scores.reason: Shows citation-faithfulness numbers depend on verifier strictness (3-18% on identical outputs) and provides a calibrated conformal guard — directly moves the belief on what grounding benchmarks can legitimately support (C3) and how to bound trustworthiness (C4), on the very benchmarks the brief names.

Purpose-built citation-grounding benchmark on scientific papers that rewards grounded refusal and shows citation metrics separate models where LLM-judge scores compress — hits C3, C4 and C5 with cross-model results.

Demonstrates that existing claim-verification benchmarks reward a salient-constraint shortcut and cannot distinguish it from genuine verification — exactly the benchmark-inflation finding the premise asks the scan to reach for (C3, C5).
Directly measures claim-evidence extraction and linking accuracy on full papers across six models and prompting strategies against annotated pairs — the closest match to question 1 (C1) in the list.

Expert-annotated claim-verification benchmark whose refutations are built by perturbing evidence rather than claims, explicitly addressing artifact-resistant construction (C3) and exposing figure/table evidence-linking failures (C2).

Relevant to extraction failure but the 0/350 strict-gate figure measures schema/format validity of reasoning graphs, not claim accuracy against expert annotation; the why_it_matters overstates its bearing on the brief's premise, though the failure taxonomy is genuinely useful for C2.
Explicitly named in the brief's known papers; its 4-18% model vs 70% human accuracy on citation attribution is core evidence for how badly evidence-linking fails (C2, C3).

Benchmarks citation attribution across 12 domains with hallucination rates and a measured mitigation, informing C2/C3 — though sentence-to-title/author attribution is a step removed from claim-evidence grounding from full papers.

Foundational slot: ALCE is the canonical automatic citation-quality benchmark whose metrics later scientific-grounding work builds on; a newcomer reading the newer benchmarks without it would misread what citation-quality numbers mean.

Foundational slot: the canonical human audit establishing base rates of unsupported citations (51.5% sentence support) — real, worth-knowing background for citation grounding, though its web-search setting makes it less essential than ALCE for this specific list.
